title: 3-D Objects: Polyhedra, Faces, Edges, Vertices and Nets
seo_title: Grade 7 3-D Objects Worksheets with Answers (CAPS Maths)
standard_text: Describe, sort and compare polyhedra in terms of the shape and number of faces, number of vertices and number of edges; revise properties and definitions of the five Platonic solids; use nets to create models of geometric solids, including cubes and prisms.
meta_desc: Free CAPS Grade 7 3-D objects worksheets: polyhedra, faces, edges and vertices, Euler's formula and nets. 100 questions with memos.
body_html:
How to think about it

  • A polyhedron is a 3-D object with flat faces: prisms and pyramids are polyhedra.
  • A prism is named after its end face; a pyramid after its base.
  • Euler: faces + vertices − edges = 2. A cube: 6 + 8 − 12 = 2.
  • A net folds up to make the object; a cube has 11 different nets.

Examples

Example

A pentagonal pyramid

1 pentagon + 5 triangles

6 vertices, 10 edges

Answer: 6 faces

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
Named after the sidesUse the end face or base.
Visible faces onlyCount the hidden faces.
Overlapping netEach face needs its own place.

items.q: Name this prism.
items.e: A prism is named after its cross-section, the shape of its two matching ends. The two ends are triangles, so it is a triangular prism. Do not name it by its 5 faces: that would give “pentagonal”.

items.q: What is the name of this prism?
items.e: A prism is named after its cross-section, the shape of its two matching ends. The ends are right-angled triangles. They are still triangles, so it is a triangular prism.

items.q: This object is a prism. What is its name?
items.e: A prism is named after its cross-section, the shape of its two matching ends. The ends are rectangles, so it is a rectangular prism. It has 6 faces, but “hexagonal” would mean the ends are hexagons.

items.q: Name this prism.
items.e: A prism is named after its cross-section, the shape of its two matching ends. The ends are squares and the long faces are rectangles, so it is a rectangular prism (also called a square prism). It is not a cube, because not all its faces are squares.

items.q: What is the name of this prism?
items.e: A prism is named after its cross-section, the shape of its two matching ends. Count the sides of an end: 5 sides, so it is a pentagonal prism. 7 is its number of faces.

items.q: This object is a prism. What is its name?
items.e: A prism is named after its cross-section, the shape of its two matching ends. The end looks like a house: a square with a triangle on top. Count its sides: 5. So it is a pentagonal prism, not a triangular prism.

items.q: Name this prism.
items.e: A prism is named after its cross-section, the shape of its two matching ends. Each end has 6 sides, so it is a hexagonal prism. 8 is its number of faces.

items.q: What is the name of this prism?
items.e: A prism is named after its cross-section, the shape of its two matching ends. Each end has 8 sides, so it is an octagonal prism. 10 is its number of faces.

items.q: This object is a prism. What is its name?
items.e: A prism is named after its cross-section, the shape of its two matching ends. This prism stands on one of its ends. The top and bottom are triangles, so it is a triangular prism.

items.q: Name this prism.
items.e: A prism is named after its cross-section, the shape of its two matching ends. The top and bottom are matching hexagons joined by rectangles, so it is a hexagonal prism.

items.q: This net is folded up. What solid does it make?
items.e: There is 1 square (the base) and 4 triangles that meet at the top. They fold into a square pyramid.

items.e: There is 1 square (the base) and 4 triangles that meet at the top. They fold into a square pyramid.

items.e: There are 6 squares that are all the same size. They fold into a cube.

items.q: This net is folded up. What solid does it make?
items.e: There are 6 rectangles in 3 matching pairs (not all squares). They fold into a rectangular prism.

items.q: A net has 2 triangles and 3 rectangles. What solid does it fold into?
items.e: There are 2 triangles (the bases) and 3 rectangles. They fold into a triangular prism.

items.q: This is a triangular prism. How many faces does it have?
items.e: A triangular prism has 5 faces (2 triangles + 3 rectangles), 9 edges (3 + 3 + 3) and 6 vertices (3 + 3). You can see only 3 faces, but the bottom and the back end count too.

items.q: This is a triangular prism. How many edges does it have?
items.e: A triangular prism has 5 faces (2 triangles + 3 rectangles), 9 edges (3 + 3 + 3) and 6 vertices (3 + 3). 3 edges round each end and 3 joining the ends.

items.q: How many vertices does a triangular prism have?
items.e: A triangular prism has 5 faces (2 triangles + 3 rectangles), 9 edges (3 + 3 + 3) and 6 vertices (3 + 3).

items.q: This is a rectangular prism. How many edges does it have?
items.e: A rectangular prism has 6 faces (2 rectangles + 4 rectangles), 12 edges (4 + 4 + 4) and 8 vertices (4 + 4). Dashed lines show edges at the back that you cannot see.

items.q: This is a pentagonal prism. How many faces does it have?
items.e: A pentagonal prism has 7 faces (2 pentagons + 5 rectangles), 15 edges (5 + 5 + 5) and 10 vertices (5 + 5). Dashed lines show edges at the back that you cannot see.

items.q: How many edges does a pentagonal prism have?
items.e: A pentagonal prism has 7 faces (2 pentagons + 5 rectangles), 15 edges (5 + 5 + 5) and 10 vertices (5 + 5). Do not forget the 5 edges that join the two ends.

items.q: This is a pentagonal prism. How many vertices does it have?
items.e: A pentagonal prism has 7 faces (2 pentagons + 5 rectangles), 15 edges (5 + 5 + 5) and 10 vertices (5 + 5).

items.q: This is a hexagonal prism. How many faces does it have?
items.e: A hexagonal prism has 8 faces (2 hexagons + 6 rectangles), 18 edges (6 + 6 + 6) and 12 vertices (6 + 6). Do not forget the 2 hexagon ends.

items.q: How many edges does a hexagonal prism have?
items.e: A hexagonal prism has 8 faces (2 hexagons + 6 rectangles), 18 edges (6 + 6 + 6) and 12 vertices (6 + 6). Edges round both ends (6 + 6) plus 6 joining them.

items.q: This is a hexagonal prism. How many vertices does it have?
items.e: A hexagonal prism has 8 faces (2 hexagons + 6 rectangles), 18 edges (6 + 6 + 6) and 12 vertices (6 + 6).

items.q: This is a cube. How many vertices does it have?
items.e: A cube has 6 square faces, 12 edges and 8 vertices. Vertices are the corners: 4 at the front and 4 at the back.

items.q: This is a rectangular prism. How many faces does it have?
items.e: A rectangular prism has 6 rectangular faces, 12 edges and 8 vertices. You can see only 3 faces. The bottom, the back and one side are hidden, but they still count.

items.q: How many edges does a rectangular prism have?
items.e: A rectangular prism has 6 rectangular faces, 12 edges and 8 vertices. There are 4 edges on the top, 4 on the bottom and 4 going up the sides.

items.q: This is a triangular prism. How many faces does it have?
items.e: A triangular prism has 5 faces (2 triangles and 3 rectangles), 9 edges and 6 vertices. Dashed lines show the edges at the back that you cannot see.

items.q: This is a triangular prism. How many edges does it have?
items.e: A triangular prism has 5 faces (2 triangles and 3 rectangles), 9 edges and 6 vertices. 3 edges round each triangle end and 3 long edges joining them: 3 + 3 + 3 = 9.

items.q: This is a square-based pyramid. How many faces does it have?
items.e: A square-based pyramid has 5 faces (1 square and 4 triangles), 8 edges and 5 vertices. Do not forget the square base underneath.

items.q: This is a square-based pyramid. How many edges does it have?
items.e: A square-based pyramid has 5 faces (1 square and 4 triangles), 8 edges and 5 vertices. 4 edges round the base and 4 going up to the top: 4 + 4 = 8.

items.q: How many vertices does a square-based pyramid have?
items.e: A square-based pyramid has 5 faces (1 square and 4 triangles), 8 edges and 5 vertices. 4 corners on the base and 1 at the top: 4 + 1 = 5.

items.q: This is a triangular pyramid. How many faces does it have?
items.e: A triangular pyramid has 4 triangular faces, 6 edges and 4 vertices. Do not forget the triangle base underneath.

items.q: How many edges does a triangular pyramid have?
items.e: A triangular pyramid has 4 triangular faces, 6 edges and 4 vertices. 3 edges round the base and 3 going up to the top: 3 + 3 = 6.

items.e: With the square at A, the 6 squares fold onto 6 different faces. At each of the other places, two squares would fold onto the same face and one face would be left open.

items.q: Does this pattern fold into a cube?
c: Yes, it folds into a cube
No, two squares land on the same face
items.e: Yes. Fold the squares one at a time: they cover all 6 faces of the cube with no overlaps. A cube has 6 faces, so its net has 6 squares (8 is the number of vertices and 12 the number of edges).

items.q: How many of these patterns are nets of a cube?
items.e: Fold each one in your head. A, C and D fold into a cube. B does not: two of its squares fold onto the same face, so one face of the cube is left open.

items.q: How many different nets does a cube have? (A net that is only turned or flipped over counts as the same net.)
items.e: A cube has 11 different nets. 6 is the number of faces, 12 the number of edges and 8 the number of vertices.

items.q: Which 3D object does this net fold into?
items.e: 6 rectangles in 3 matching pairs fold into a rectangular prism. Opposite faces are the same size.

items.q: What object can be made from this net?
items.e: 2 triangles (the bases) and 3 rectangles fold into a triangular prism. The bases are right triangles here; a prism’s bases do not have to be equilateral.

items.q: This net is folded up. Which object does it make?
items.e: 1 square base and 4 triangles that meet at one point fold into a square-based pyramid.

items.q: Which 3D object does this net fold into?
items.e: 4 triangles fold into a triangular pyramid: one is the base and the other 3 meet at a point.

items.q: What object can be made from this net?
items.e: 2 pentagons (the bases) and 5 rectangles fold into a pentagonal prism.

items.q: This net is folded up. Which object does it make?
items.e: 1 hexagon base and 6 triangles that meet at one point fold into a hexagonal pyramid. A pyramid is named after its base.

items.q: Which 3D object does this net fold into?
items.e: 1 rectangle base and 4 triangles that meet at one point fold into a rectangular pyramid. The base is a rectangle that is not a square, so the triangles on the long sides and short sides differ.

items.q: What object can be made from this net?
items.e: 1 pentagon base and 5 triangles that meet at one point fold into a pentagonal pyramid.

items.q: This net is folded up. Which object does it make?
items.e: 2 hexagons (the bases) and 6 rectangles fold into a hexagonal prism.

items.q: Which net folds into a pentagonal prism?
items.e: A has 2 pentagons on opposite edges of a strip of 5 rectangles. One wrong net is a pentagonal pyramid, one has only 4 rectangles (it cannot close), and one has both pentagons on the same edge, so they fold onto the same end.

items.q: Which 3-D shape does this net make?
items.e: There are 6 squares that are all the same size. They fold into a cube.

items.e: There are 6 rectangles in 3 matching pairs, and they are not all squares. They fold into a cuboid.

items.q: This net is folded up. What shape does it make?
items.e: There are 4 triangles and nothing else. They fold into a tetrahedron (a triangular-based pyramid).

items.q: Which of these is NOT a net of a cube?
items.e: B is not a net of a cube: two squares are on the same side of the row of 4, so they fold onto the same face and one face is left open. The other three each fold into a cube.

items.q: Which of these is NOT a net of a cube?
items.e: A is not a net of a cube: 5 squares in a row wrap all the way round, so the first and last squares overlap. The other three each fold into a cube.

items.q: Nomsa’s family tent has two triangle ends, two sloping sides and a floor. What object is the tent shaped like?
items.e: Two triangle ends joined by rectangles (2 sides and the floor) make a triangular prism. Do not use the 5 faces to name it.

items.q: A chocolate bar comes in a long box with two triangle ends. Tebogo flattens the box for recycling. How many faces of cardboard are there?
items.e: The box is a triangular prism: 2 triangles + 3 rectangles = 5 faces. 9 is the number of edges.

items.q: Ruan’s pencil is a hexagonal prism. How many long flat faces run down its side (not counting the ends)?
items.e: A hexagon has 6 sides, so there are 6 rectangles along the pencil. 8 counts the 2 ends as well, and 3 is how many you can see at once.

items.q: Tumi makes the frame of a hexagonal prism from straws, one straw for each edge. How many straws does she need?
items.e: Edges: 6 round each end + 6 joining them = 18. 12 is the number of vertices and 8 the number of faces.

items.q: Daniel uses balls of modelling clay to join straws at the corners of a pentagonal prism. How many balls of clay does he need?
items.e: One ball for each vertex: 5 on each pentagon end, 5 + 5 = 10. 15 is the number of edges.

items.q: Siyabonga paints each face of a wooden triangular prism a different colour. How many colours does he use?
items.e: A triangular prism has 2 triangles + 3 rectangles = 5 faces.

items.q: Andile stacks 10 identical hexagon tiles exactly on top of each other. What object does the stack look like?
items.e: Every layer is the same hexagon, so the stack has the same cross-section all the way up: a hexagonal prism.

items.q: Kyle stacks square tiles, each one smaller than the one below, with their centres in a line. Which object is the stack most like?
items.e: The square cross-sections get smaller towards the top, like a square-based pyramid. In a prism they would all be the same size.

items.q: Bongani’s birdhouse has a front and a back shaped like a house (a square with a triangle roof), joined by rectangles. What object is it?
items.e: The house shape has 5 sides, so the birdhouse is a pentagonal prism.

items.q: Liam says the Great Pyramid of Giza is a prism. Why is he wrong?
c: Its cross-sections get smaller towards the top
It is too big to be a prism
items.e: The Great Pyramid is a square-based pyramid: its square slices shrink to a point. A prism keeps the same cross-section all the way up.

items.q: This net is folded into a cube. Which face is opposite face A?
items.e: Faces A and C are in a straight line with one square between them, so they fold onto opposite sides of the cube.

items.q: This net is folded into a cube. Which face is opposite face C?
items.e: Faces C and A are in a straight line with one square between them, so they fold onto opposite sides of the cube.

items.q: This net is folded into a cube with face C on the bottom. Which face is on the top?
items.e: Fold the net: face A lands opposite face C. A face that touches C in the net (B, F) is next to it on the cube, never opposite.

items.q: This net is folded into a cube with face D on the bottom. Which face is on the top?
items.e: Faces D and C are in a straight line with one square between them, so they fold onto opposite sides of the cube.

items.q: This net is folded into a cube. Which face does NOT touch face A?
items.e: Faces A and F are in a straight line with one square between them, so they fold onto opposite sides of the cube.

items.q: This net is folded into a rectangular prism. Which face is opposite face Q?
items.e: Faces Q and S are the same size and have one face (R) between them in the strip, so they fold onto opposite sides. In a rectangular prism, opposite faces are always the same size and shape.

items.q: In the net, face A touches only 1 other face. When the net is folded into a cube, how many faces will touch face A?
items.e: On a cube, every face touches 4 other faces. Only the opposite face (face F) does not touch it.

items.q: This is a net of a dice. The numbers on opposite faces add up to 7. What number goes on the face marked ?
items.e: When the net is folded, the face marked ? is opposite the 6. So the missing number is 7 − 6 = 1.

items.q: This is a net of a dice. The numbers on opposite faces add up to 7. What number goes on the face marked ?
items.e: When the net is folded, the face marked ? is opposite the 1. So the missing number is 7 − 1 = 6.

items.q: This net is folded into a cube. Which 3 faces meet at the corner with the red dot?
items.e: Every corner of a cube is where 3 faces meet. In the net the dot touches F; when you fold the net, A and C fold up to the same corner, so the 3 faces are A, C and F.
